producer_original_scope_boundaries.purpose: Boundary record for reuse of this material. Lists only conditions actually present in the native source. Nothing here adds, strengthens or weakens the authors' hypotheses.

necessary_conditions.label: Assumption (H_delta)
content: Stationarity and ergodicity of the random set Ic
Uniform C^2 regularity: random shapes I_n^o satisfy interior and exterior ball conditions with the same radius delta, almost surely
Uniform hardcore condition: (I_n^+ + delta B) intersect (I_m^+ + delta B) = empty for all n != m, almost surely
shapes I_n^o are connected random Borel subsets of the unit ball B, centered at 0 in the sense that the first moment vanishes (line 252)
I_n = x_n + I_n^o with x_n the barycenter; Ic = union of I_n; I_n^+ is the convex hull (line 253-254)
necessary_conditions.used_by: all candidates; the only probabilistic+geometric input for C2, C3 and for the quenched part of C4

necessary_conditions.label: Assumption (Mix^+)
content: A non-increasing weight function pi on R^+ with superalgebraic decay, i.e. pi(l) <= C_p <l>^{-p} for all p < infty
multiscale variance inequality Var{Y(Ic)} <= E[ int_0^infty int_{R^d} (partial^osc_{Ic,B_l(x)} Y)^2 dx <l>^{-d} pi(l) dl ] for all sigma(Ic)-measurable Y
the oscillation is the essential-sup/inf over realizations agreeing with Ic outside the ball B_l(x)
necessary_conditions.used_by: C1 (th:cor, th:cor+ and prop:CLTscaling, via lem:p), the r_* moment bound in C4, C5
necessary_conditions.not_used_by: C2, C3, and the quenched statements th:schauder / th:lp-reg (which only need Hd)

necessary_conditions.literal: we denote by d >= 2 the space dimension
necessary_conditions.note: Mu_d in eq:bnd-cor also carries a d=1 branch, included for completeness per remark 320-322 (see notation points).

content: D(u_eps) = 0 inside eps Ic, i.e. u_eps is a linearized rigid motion V_{eps,n} + Theta_{eps,n}(x - eps x_n) in each particle
zero force: int_{eps partial I_n} sigma(u_eps,P_eps) nu = 0
zero torque: int_{eps partial I_n} Theta(x - eps x_n) . sigma(u_eps,P_eps) nu = 0 for all skew-symmetric Theta
same structure for the corrector (eq:corr-Stokes) and for the whole-space test problem (eq:test-v0), where the forcing g enters the boundary conditions as int (g + sigma) nu = 0
necessary_conditions.note: The buoyancy-free condition ('particles have the same mass density as the fluid') is the physical hypothesis behind zero force/torque (line 145-146). The sedimentation variant replaces force balance by a constant gravity term (line 179-181) and is outside this article.

content: div u_eps = 0 in U minus eps Ic
Stokes stress sigma(u,P) = 2 D(u) - P Id (eq:eq:Cauchy, line 152-153)

pressure is only defined up to a constant: the article normalizes int_{U minus Ic_eps(U)} P_eps = 0 in eq:Stokes (line 424), int_U Pbar = 0 (line 433), int_{D_R} P 1_{R^d minus Ic} = int_{D_R} Phat = 0 (line 1624), fint_B psi_E = 0 and fint_B zeta_E = 0 as anchoring
in the two-scale error, the pressure error is measured modulo inf over kappa in R (eq:hom-quant0, line 443)

necessary_conditions.literal: In view of quantitative homogenization results, we need to further consider quantitative ergodicity assumptions, which we make here for convenience in form of the multiscale variance inequality
necessary_conditions.note: This is the only quantitative mixing input; no spectral-gap or other mixing formulation is used or assumed in this paper.

whole_space_vs_finite_volume: Correctors are defined on the whole space R^d as infinite-volume limits with an anchoring condition (lem:cor, lem:ext-cor); stationarity and finite second moments are part of the statements.
C3 and the regularity theory are set on the whole space R^d with g in C^infty_c; the local statements in prop:Meyers item (ii) are on a ball D with particle conditions only for I_n contained in D.
C5 is the finite-volume result: smooth bounded U, particles selected by eps(I_n^+ + delta B) subset U, particles meeting the boundary excluded (line 402).
Large-scale estimates are restricted to scales at least r_*(0) (or r_*(x) with B_*(x)) and at most R; r_* is an almost surely finite stationary random field defined by eq:e.def-r*.
epsilon_limits: eps down to 0 with fixed volume fraction lambda = E[1_Ic]; the dilute regime is not the regime of this paper (a deterministic dilute variant is the separate omitted remark rem:reg-hofer)
rate for C5: (eps mu_d(1/eps))^{1/2} in general; eps mu_d(1/eps) when f and ubar are compactly supported in U (line 453)
logarithmic degradation is confined to mu_d and only for d <= 2: mu_d = 1 for d>2, log(2+r)^{1/2} for d=2, <r>^{1/2} for d=1
in p1 there is a competing term (R/r)^{d+2} (1 wedge gamma_R)^{2 eps_exp}: it is small only when gamma_R is small, which is exactly the minimal-radius condition
regularity_classes: correctors: psi_E in H^1_loc(R^d)^d with Sigma_E in L^2_loc(R^d minus Ic); zeta_E in H^1_loc for each component; J_E a stationary 2-tensor with finite second moment
test forcing for the regularity theory: g in C^infty_c(R^d; L^infty(Omega)^{d x d})
C5 forcing: f in W^{1+alpha,infty}(U)^d, alpha>0; solutions (u_eps,P_eps) in L^infty(Omega; H^1_0(U)^d x L^2(U minus Ic_eps(U)))
Muckenhoupt weights A_p (and A_2 for the weighted Bogovskii lemma) appear only in th:lp-reg, th:ann-reg and Substep 3.1 of the p1 proof
constants_dependence: the generic constant C >= 1 depends only on d, on delta in (H_delta), on the weight pi in (Mix+) if applicable, and on the reference domain U (line 237); subscripts record further dependence
C_0 ~ 1 in the Meyers statements depends on (d, delta); C_alpha ~_alpha 1 in th:excess-decay; rate constant in C5 depends on alpha and q

core_dedup_boundaries.rule_applied: Statements sharing one corrector/randomized-estimate core or one excess-decay core were not split; only statements with their own new analytic burden were kept.
merged_into_C1: th:cor and th:cor+ (same moment bounds, extended to zeta)
prop:CLTscaling and prop:interpol (the two estimates that the buckling argument combines)
merged_into_C4: p1 (the core), th:excess-decay (Campanato iteration referred to GNO-reg), th:schauder (referred to GNO-reg Cor. 3), th:lp-reg (Shen CZ as in DO1), th:ann-reg (Shen CZ as in DO1, plus C3's perturbative clause)
merged_into_C3: th:meyers-ann and its deterministic engine prop:Meyers, together with the auxiliary lemmas lem:reform-whole and lem:pres
kept_separate_though_dependent: C2 (extended flux / flux corrector): separately stated, separately proved, used by both C1 and C5
C3 vs C4: different mechanisms (deterministic Gehring/CZ in a small exponent window vs quenched excess decay)
C5 vs C1/C2/C4: distinct statement (bounded-domain error rate, two error norms, infimum over kappa) with its own boundary-layer and divergence-corrector analysis
not_counted: lem:Shen, lem:Gehring, lem:p, lem:muck: quoted lemmas with no proof in this article
lem:cor: quoted corrector existence from DG-19, used as a definitional input
rem at line 320-322: a completeness comment on d=1
